agency: Delaware Department of Health and Social Services (DHSS), Division of Social Services (DSS)
admin_note: Delaware is a STATE-ADMINISTERED SNAP program — DHSS's Division of Social Services (DSS) administers directly through State Service Centers, with no county-level policy variation, structurally similar to this roster's Nebraska, Connecticut, North Carolina, Ohio, New Jersey, Tennessee, Indiana, Missouri, Maryland, Colorado, South Carolina, Alabama, Louisiana, Kentucky, Oklahoma, Utah, Iowa, Arkansas, Mississippi, Kansas, New Mexico, and New Hampshire packs. GENUINE STRUCTURAL FLAGSHIP FINDING: Delaware's own current regulatory text (the Division of Social Services Manual, DSSM) is genuinely BEHIND currently-operative Delaware SNAP policy in at least three separately-confirmed places — this pack fetched DSSM 9045's own resource-limit text ($2,000 general / $3,000 elderly-disabled, unamended since at least 2009) and found it below the current federal FY2026 COLA-adjusted floor of $3,000/$4,500 that 7 CFR 273.8(a) requires; DSSM 9018.2/9018.3's ABAWD age-exemption text (under 18, age 50+) is the pre-OBBBA standard, while DHSS's own live SNAP Alert consumer page confirms the current post-11/1/2025 OBBBA standard (ages 18-64, child under 14, no homeless/veteran/foster-youth exemption); and DSSM 9013.2 still cross-references "DSSM 2027" as an active drug-felony ineligibility category, even though DSSM 2027 itself was fully REPEALED effective March 11, 2018 (21 DE Reg. 722). This pack treats DHSS's live, actively-maintained consumer pages (SNAP page, SNAP Alert) as the source of currently-operative policy over the DSSM's own stale cross-references and unamended dollar figures wherever the two conflict, and flags each instance explicitly rather than silently picking one. SECOND FLAGSHIP FINDING, a genuine primary-source CONFIRMATION reached by chasing a specific repealed-regulation citation rather than accepting secondary-source paraphrase: several secondary sources describe Delaware as having a 'modified' drug-felony SNAP ban requiring sentence compliance; this pack fetched Delaware's own DSSM 2027 text directly and found it fully REPEALED (21 DE Reg. 722, effective 3/11/2018), removing the drug-felony restriction from Cash Assistance/General Assistance entirely, with SNAP's own DSSM 9042.2 categorical-eligibility exclusion list containing no drug-felony exclusion category at all — Delaware has FULLY opted out of the federal drug-felony SNAP ban, not merely modified it. THIRD FINDING: Delaware's SNAP categorical-eligibility gate (DSSM 9042) is triggered by a non-cash TANF-funded pregnancy-prevention-information service at 200% FPL gross income, exempting the large majority of DE households from any resource test — structurally the same BBCE mechanism family as this roster's New Hampshire pack, but implemented through a distinctive pregnancy-prevention-information authorization line embedded directly in Delaware's own SNAP application form; see income-and-resources supplement. Confirm current operative practice with the applicant's own local DSS State Service Center, the same caution this roster already carries for its other built states.
system: DHHS's Division of Social Services (DSS) processes SNAP centrally (no county offices with independent policy authority); applicants apply online through Delaware ASSIST (assist.dhss.delaware.gov), or in person at any Delaware State Service Center. The Food Bank of Delaware operates a DSS-adjacent SNAP Outreach program assisting with applications. Delaware's standard certification period is 12 months, extended to 24 months for households where all members are elderly (60+) or disabled with no earned income. Delaware's own DSSM regulatory text is flagged in this pack as lagging currently-operative DHSS policy in several specific, confirmed places, see freshness.json.

verification.method: dhss.delaware.gov and regulations.delaware.gov both returned clean HTTP 200 to direct curl attempts with a standard browser User-Agent — no WAF/bot-detection barrier of the kind this roster's New Hampshire and Maine packs encountered. The one genuine access wrinkle this pack hit was regulations.delaware.gov's SPA front-end: the human-facing /AdminCode/titleNN/NNNN URLs render client-side JavaScript with no server-rendered content, so this pack located and fetched the underlying /api/AdminCode/titleNN/NNNN/<uuid> PDF endpoints directly instead (found via WebSearch, not by reverse-engineering the SPA), and used pdftotext -layout on the resulting 114-page DSSM 9000 PDF and the archived DSSM 2000 PDF. Both fetched cleanly with no staleness concerns about the fetch mechanism itself. The one genuine data-freshness finding in this pack is internal to Delaware's own regulatory text, not a fetch-tooling artifact: the DSSM's own dollar figures and cross-references (resource limits at DSSM 9045, ABAWD age exemptions at DSSM 9018.2/9018.3, and the drug-felony cross-reference at DSSM 9013.2) are demonstrably behind DHSS's own live, actively-maintained consumer pages and the Delaware Register of Regulations' own repeal order — this pack resolved every one of these conflicts by taking DHSS's live consumer pages and the dated Register of Regulations order as authoritative over the DSSM's own unamended cross-references, and discloses each instance explicitly in freshness.json and PROVENANCE.md rather than silently picking a number.
